question: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of pain and swelling in his right knee that began 3 days ago when he fell during football practice. He fell on his flexed right knee as he dove to complete a pass. He felt some mild knee pain but continued to practice. Over the next 2 days, the pain worsened and the knee began to swell. Today, the patient has an antalgic gait. Examination shows a swollen and tender right knee; flexion is limited by pain. The right knee is flexed and pressure is applied to proximal tibia; 8 mm of backward translation of the foreleg is observed. Which of the following is most likely injured?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fall during football practice" -> "Flexed right knee injury" -> "Mild knee pain initially" -> "Continued practice despite pain" -> "Worsening pain and swelling over 2 days" -> "Antalgic gait observed" -> "Swollen and tender right knee on examination" -> "Limited flexion due to pain" -> "8 mm of backward translation of the foreleg with pressure on proximal tibia" -> "Most likely injured structure: Posterior cruciate ligament" -> 95%
analysis: Based on the mechanism of injury described and the physical examination findings of posterior translation of the tibia on the femur, the most likely injured structure is the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL). The PCL prevents posterior translation of the tibia on the femur.
